citations.M3: right after step 1 every existing row has `state=NULL`, so `OrderState(row["state"])` raises on every single order read until backfill catches that row
citations.M4: The `MAPPING` CASE has no ELSE — `'PAID'`, `'canceled'`, `'complete'`, and NULL statuses (7,764 prod rows) map to NULL forever
citations.M6: The backfill wraps the entire loop in one transaction — on 61M rows that's a long-held transaction risking WAL/replica bloat and an all-or-nothing rollback
citations.M7: `jobs/nightly_finance_export.py` still selects `o.status` and isn't touched by this PR — the grep was scoped to `app/` and missed `jobs/`
citations.M12: `alter_column(..., nullable=False)` on a 61M-row table forces a full-table scan under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, blocking all reads/writes for its duration
